name: PityTimer
src_typeComment: Bad-luck protection ("pity timer"): each failed roll increases the effective chance, guaranteeing a success within guaranteedAfter attempts instead of letting pure independent rolls occasionally streak far longer than feels fair — the classic gacha/loot-box design pattern. Plain C# class (not a MonoBehaviour) so a system with several independent pity counters (e.g. one per loot table) can just hold a field of these rather than needing a GameObject per counter.

src_serialized.name: baseChance
src_serialized.tooltip: Base chance of success on any single roll, before pity increases it.

src_serialized.name: guaranteedAfter
src_serialized.tooltip: A roll is guaranteed to succeed once this many consecutive failures have accumulated.

src_serialized.name: failCount
src_serialized.tooltip: Consecutive failures so far. Serialized so pity progress survives a save; set it from LoadFailCount when restoring.
src_serialized.comment: SERIALIZED, not an auto-property. The whole point of a pity timer is that bad luck carries across sessions: as a { get; private set; } auto-property this was invisible to Unity's serializer, so the CONFIG saved and the player's accumulated progress toward the guarantee did not - exactly backwards for the gacha case the class is named after.

src_members.sig: public void LoadFailCount(int value) => failCount = Mathf.Clamp(value, 0, Mathf.Max(1, guaranteedAfter) - 1)
src_members.name: LoadFailCount
src_members.comment: Restores accumulated pity from a save. Clamped, because a value at or beyond the guarantee would make the next roll a certainty regardless of what the save actually meant.
